stem: A healthcare study measures average patient recovery rate across 4 hospitals, each containing multiple departments. hospital A has 15 observations with mean 66.3 % (within-hospital SD = 7.7). hospital B has 20 observations with mean 56.5 % (within-hospital SD = 7.2). hospital C has 5 observations with mean 57.3 % (within-hospital SD = 7.9). hospital D has 10 observations with mean 63.5 % (within-hospital SD = 4.5). The between-hospital standard deviation is uncertain, estimated between 8.7 and 21.8 %. Using a hierarchical Bayesian model, estimate the true average patient recovery rate for hospital C, accounting for shrinkage toward the grand mean and the uncertainty in the between-hospital variation.

ground_truth.answer: Hierarchical estimate for hospital C: 57.5 % (shrunk from raw 57.3). Range [57.4, 57.8] as between-hospital SD varies from 8.7 to 21.8. Pooled mean: 60.9.

solution_steps: Compute pooled (grand) mean: 60.9 % (weighted average of 4 hospital means).
Shrinkage factor for hospital C: B = σ²_between / (σ²_between + σ²_within/5). At σ_between=14.5: B = 0.944.
Interval [57.4, 57.8] captures uncertainty from the unknown between-group variance.
common_failure_modes: Using the raw observed mean (57.3) without shrinkage
Using only the grand mean (60.9) and ignoring group-specific data
Not recognizing that small-sample groups should be shrunk more toward the grand mean
Treating the between-group variance as known rather than uncertain
